question: E4e: does the state of the river at the issue time (hourly USGS gauge flow: the flow at local midnight relative to Q95, its 6- and 12-hour change, the day's peak hour and the hours above Q95) make the all-river LSTM warn of more flood onsets 1 day ahead on the satellite-era split, alone, with the within-day AORC rain, and with the GEFS forecast; and how much is lost when the record stops two hours before the issue time?

split_text: the satellite-era split (train 2000-10-01..2008-09-30, validation 2008-10-01..2010-09-30, test 2010-10-01..2014-09-30; flood thresholds from its training years; its numbers are comparable only inside it)
outcome: Given the state of the river at the issue time from the gauge's own 15-minute record reduced to hours (the flow at local midnight relative to Q95, its change over the last 6 and 12 hours, the day's highest hourly flow and the hours above Q95) as five extra inputs beside the AORC rain to midnight to the LSTM with the river gauge, on the satellite-era split (train 2000-10-01..2008-09-30, validation 2008-10-01..2010-09-30, test 2010-10-01..2014-09-30; flood thresholds from its training years; its numbers are comparable only inside it), onsets warned 1 day ahead go from 41% with the AORC rain to midnight alone (lstm_wqa_s, stored) to 47% (single trainings 46% to 48%; the onsets of one storm are not independent): +6.6 points (159 against 137 hits of 335); with the last available hour ending 22:00 instead of 24:00, 43% (single trainings 40% to 46%); the share of false warnings among the onset warnings is 38% against 55%; the median NSE goes from 0.71 to 0.80 (the seed-averaged forecast; single trainings 0.77 to 0.81); the verdict of results/flood_analysis.json at trigger 1.0 is NOT YET for the onsets and GO for all high-flow days.
outcome_caveat: The success rule fixed before training (wqaH_s above wqa_s in every seed at lead 1 on this split) is not met with the five seeds and would be with the first three (seeds 0, 1, 2): the verdict depends on the seed count (five seeds were chosen at launch with --seeds 5, the script's default being three, in one training pass before any test score was seen): the five single trainings with the river's state span 45.7% to 48.4% against 33.1% to 46.9% without it (seeds 3, 4 of wqaH_s are not above the best wqa_s seed); 41 onsets are warned only with it against 19 only without it. With the six within-day AORC rain columns beside it (wqaWH_s) 59% (single trainings 56% to 61%); with the GEFS forecast as well (wqaWHF_s against the stored lstm_wqaF_s) 1-day onsets warned go from 61% to 68% (single trainings 62% to 74% against 57% to 65%: no clear difference by the seed rule, so the +7.2 points rest on the seed-averaged forecast and on the paired onsets: 49 warned only with the new columns against 25 only without, sign test p = 0.007, a description only; false 39% against 47%), at 2 and 3 days from 49% to 48% and from 44% to 45%. Delivery: with the record ending 22:00 instead of 24:00, onsets warned 1 day ahead are 4.8 points below the 24:00 variant in the river-only sets, 2.1 points below with the within-day rain and 1.8 points above with the forecast as well, all inside the seed spread at every lead (no family separates its 24:00 and 22:00 variants seed by seed at any lead). The five columns close 21% of the gap in onsets warned from wqa_s (41%) to the perfect rain forecast in the slots (wqaP_s, 72%, an upper bound that cannot be had in practice) and 95% of the gap in median NSE. At the 30%-false operating point (the trigger chosen on the validation years so that at most 30% of the onset warnings are false: 1.20) wqaH_s warns of 38% with 25% false on the test years, against 15% with 24% false for wqa_s (trigger 1.50). The hourly record has gaps: on 1786 of the 64644 basin-days (768 in the test years) the five columns fall back to the daily mean (hourly_known = 0); the hourly flow is the gauge's own record, an input a real-time service has as provisional values and after a delivery delay (the 24:00 variant assumes none and the 22:00 variant two hours; this study used the approved record), while the AORC rain to midnight is an analysis made after the fact (hindsight at most about 3 points, a bound measured for the daily total only); the within-day columns of wqaWH_s and wqaWHF_s have no such measurement. Every number of the new sets is a five-seed number; the stored sets have three seeds; the split has 335 test-year onsets and its base is weaker than the main-split wqa.

design.what: one LSTM (flood.LSTMNet, hidden 64) for all basins with the river gauge (log1p daily flow) and the basin properties (flood.STATIC), the settings of results/lstm_all.json; every set differs from the stored wqa_s only in the daily input columns listed; the trainer stops on the mean validation NSE of this split; tables from 2000-01-01 as script 18 builds them; the test years 2010-2014 are scored once

wqaH_s.what: wqa_s + the five hourly-flow columns of the issue day (the last available hour ending 24:00 local)

wqaH22_s.what: wqa_s + the five hourly-flow columns of the issue day (the last available hour ending 22:00 local)

wqaWH_s.what: wqaH_s + the six within-day AORC columns of code/subdaily_inputs.py (the last available hour ending 24:00 local)

wqaWH22_s.what: wqaH22_s + the six within-day AORC columns of code/subdaily_inputs.py (the last available hour ending 22:00 local)

wqaWHF_s.what: wqaWH_s + fc1..fc3, the bias-corrected GEFS control-member forecast of the days t+1..t+3 (script 18's columns; the last available hour ending 24:00 local)

wqaWHF22_s.what: wqaWH22_s + fc1..fc3, the bias-corrected GEFS control-member forecast of the days t+1..t+3 (script 18's columns; the last available hour ending 22:00 local)

wqa_s.what: the LSTM with the river gauge and the AORC rain to midnight on the satellite-era split (script 18, E2b): the base

wqaF_s.what: wqa_s + the bias-corrected GEFS forecast fc1..fc3 (script 18, E2b): the base of the forecast sets

wqaP_s.what: wqa_s + the AORC rain of the three target days in the slots: a perfect rain forecast, the ceiling of this split (an upper bound that cannot be had in practice)

columns.q_end: log1p(q_last of the hour ending 24:00 local / Q95)
columns.q_dmax: log1p(highest hourly mean flow of day t / Q95)
columns.hours_above: hours of day t with the hourly mean flow above Q95 (0-24; 23 or 25 where the clocks change)
columns.*_22: the same five with the last available hour ending 22:00 local (dq6 from 16:00, dq12 from 10:00)
columns.fallback: a missing hour carries the last known value for at most 6 hours; a day not wholly known after that: q_end = log1p(q_mm / Q95), dq6 = dq12 = 0, q_dmax = q_end, hours_above = last hour x (q_mm > Q95)
columns.within_day: the six columns of code/subdaily_inputs.py (hours ending at or before 24:00 of day t; aorc_maxcell1h filled with aorc_max1h where NaN)
columns.fc: fc1..fc3 = fc_bc_1..3 of data/gefs/basins (script 18's wqaF_s columns)
columns.units: mm/day over the basin, cfs x 0.0283168 x 86400 / (area_km2 x 1e6) x 1000 (code/camels.py); Q95 in mm/day; the engine standardizes every column by the training-years mean and spread

design.thresholds_source: flood.thresholds(D, split=SAT_SPLIT): the 95th percentile of the daily flow of the training years 2000-10-01..2008-09-30 of this split, per basin
design.hourly_source: code/fetch_usgs_iv.py (USGS Water Data OGC API, parameter 00060, approved 15-minute values, hour-ending UTC stamps)
design.delivery_assumptions: the 24:00 variant assumes zero delivery delay (it reads the hour that ends at the issue time) and approved values (every hourly value used is from the approved record); the 22:00 variant assumes a delivery delay of at most two hours; a real-time service gets provisional values after the gauge's telemetry delay, and neither variant covers the provisional-to-approved revision (review of 2026-10-29, must-fix 1)
design.success_rule: wqaH_s above wqa_s in every seed at lead 1 on this split: onsets warned 1 day ahead, pooled over the basins at trigger 1.0, every single seed of wqaH_s above every single seed of the stored lstm_wqa_s

data_coverage.how_to_read: per basin: the hourly source, time zone, areas, Q95, first and last hour, the gaps after 2000-01-01 (hours without 15-minute values before any carry), the approved share, the local-day mean of the hourly flow against the CAMELS daily mean, the hours carried and the days that fell back to the daily mean (both variants; also in the test years)

delivery.how_to_read: the same inputs with the last available hour of the gauge record ending at the issue time (24:00) and two hours before it (22:00), side by side, per family and lead (test years; onsets pooled at trigger 1.0; far_cap = the 30%-false operating point; the rule and the paired onsets of each pair are in readings)

closure.how_to_read: the share of the gap from the base to lstm_wqaP_s (the perfect rain forecast in the slots) that each set closes, per lead, in median NSE and in onsets warned

operating_points.how_to_read: per set and lead: plain = trigger 1.0; csi and far_cap = triggers chosen on the validation years of this split by code/warning_policy.choose_trigger (grid 0.50 to 2.00 step 0.05) and scored once on the test years (far_cap: most onsets warned with pooled onset FAR at most 0.30 on validation; reached=false: no trigger met the cap, the lowest-FAR trigger is given); the test FAR is the one that came out; test_verdict applies the GO / CAUTION / NOT YET criteria of results/flood_analysis.json

criteria.applied_to: test years, at the warning level chosen on the validation years; separately for all high-flow days and for onsets; pooled over the 12 basins and per basin; lead 1, 2, 3; for lstm_wq, lstm_w and lstm_wqf
criteria.definitions: pod = share of high-flow days that were warned; far = share of warnings that were false; csi = hits / (hits + misses + false alarms)

far_cap.note: no trigger of the grid keeps the onset false share at or below the cap on validation; the trigger with the lowest false share is given

e4e_success.rule: wqaH_s above wqa_s in every seed at lead 1 on this split: onsets warned 1 day ahead, pooled over the basins at trigger 1.0, every single seed of wqaH_s above every single seed of the stored lstm_wqa_s
e4e_success.seed_count_note: the work order names no seed count and the script's default is three; met = the rule over all 5 seeds of wqaH_s against the 3 of the stored wqa_s; met_with_first_three_seeds = the same rule with seeds 0, 1, 2 of wqaH_s only (the verdict depends on the seed count when the two differ; review of 2026-10-29, should-fix 3)

causality.what: (a) data side: the made-up-hours test on the hourly-flow columns (every basin, both variants) and code/subdaily_inputs.checks() on the within-day rain columns; (b) engine: flood.fit runs flood._assert_causal on every network before training (a trained network exists only if it passed); (c) end to end: the made-up-values test on one SAVED network per set (first seed; the new columns, then every input column and the flow, replaced by random values after a cut day: no forecast issued on or before the cut changed, later ones did); (d) every column is dated by the ISSUE day t and holds hours ending at or before the last available hour of day t

made_up_hours.what: every hourly value (mean and last, missing hours too) after the issue instant of a cut day replaced by random numbers (0 to 5000 cfs) and the columns rebuilt: no row up to the cut day changed (exact equality of all columns), the next day changed; for the 22:00 variant the issue instant is 22:00 of the cut day and the 24:00 columns of the cut day changed too

data_side.what: Checks of code/subdaily_inputs.py and the timing of the issue-day rain before the test-year onsets (written 2026-10-29)
data_side.how: code/subdaily_inputs.checks(): routes agree, window order, 23/24/25-hour days, the made-up-hours test of the within-day rain columns; record rewritten to results/diagnostics_2026-10-28/subdaily_inputs_check.json

causality.engine_check: flood._assert_causal at the start of every flood.fit

reload_check.what: one trained network per set (the first seed) rebuilt from its .pt file alone, run on the same tables, compared with the forecasts stored by save_preds (same machine; the Mac-trained stored sets are not reloaded)
reload_check.tolerance: numpy.allclose, rtol 1e-6, atol 1e-8, missing values equal

integrity.how_to_read: sha256 of every prediction set and network file of this script as they are when this file is written; made_in_this_pass lists the files this pass wrote, every other file was only read and its hash compared with the earlier results file; stored_sets_read: the files of the stored comparison sets (never written by this script)

choices_made_after_looking_at_test_score: The sets, the inputs, the stopping rule and the success rule (wqaH_s above wqa_s in every seed at lead 1 on this split) were fixed in NEXT_EXPERIMENTS_2026-10-28.md (section E4e, which names no seed count) and in this script before the first training (its sha256 is recorded at the start of every pass: 6947ffe15be6c37964f63b743646db31e538e3df00bf2ec47b629e8e1f108af9 for the training pass, passes[0].script_sha256); the five seeds were chosen at launch (--seeds 5; the script's default is three), in one training pass before any test score was seen; the test years were scored once; with the first three seeds the success rule would be met (e4e_success.met_with_first_three_seeds; the verdict depends on the seed count).
notes: Hourly flow: cfs -> mm/day with the area code/camels.py uses for the daily flow (the CAMELS forcing-file header, D[g].attrs['area_km2']), so the hourly flow sits on the scale of q_mm and Q95; area_gages2 differs from it by up to a few percent and is recorded beside it; the local-day means of the hourly flow reproduce the CAMELS daily means (data_coverage: corr and ratio per basin).

Missing hours are never filled with zero: a missing hour carries the last known value for at most 6 hours (hourly_missing_hours); a day not wholly known after that falls back to the daily mean (hourly_known = 0): 1786 basin-days in the 24:00 variant, 1791 in the 22:00 variant (data_coverage per basin). The quality columns are not inputs. aorc_maxcell1h was filled with aorc_max1h on 1 basin-days wholly filled from ERA5.
The stored sets lstm_wqa_s, lstm_wqaF_s and lstm_wqaP_s were rescored by this script's code from results/preds (checks_against_stored_results); their Mac-trained networks were not reloaded here.

Delivery assumptions (review of 2026-10-29, must-fix 1): the 24:00 variant reads the hour that ends at the issue time, so it assumes zero delivery delay, and every hourly value used is from the approved record (approved share 1.0 in every gauge, data_coverage): a real-time service gets provisional values, revised later, after the gauge's telemetry delay (the review: hourly for most USGS stations, four-hourly for some); the 22:00 variant assumes a delay of at most two hours and is the conservative one of the two only against such a delay; neither covers the provisional-to-approved revision.

Quoting. Any document must quote outcome_full (outcome plus outcome_caveat), never outcome alone; every number is a seed-averaged number unless it says 'single trainings'; the status field says whether the experiment has been reviewed.

247 values in this file are not numbers (NaN: shares whose denominator is zero, undefined p-values, the load average Windows does not have); they are written as null, which a reader must treat as 'no value'.
